summary_paragraph: An elderly woman with a history of chronic diastolic heart failure, transfusion-dependent anemia due to myelodysplastic syndrome, and recurrent venous thromboembolism on warfarin was admitted after a mechanical fall at home, resulting in left hip pain. Imaging showed no fracture on X-ray, and a CT scan revealed a subtle finding that orthopedics attributed to artifact rather than a true fracture. She was treated for a urinary tract infection caused by Klebsiella oxytoca with IV ceftriaxone, transitioning to oral cefpodoxime at discharge. During her stay, she developed hypoxia due to an acute exacerbation of diastolic heart failure, likely from recent fluid overload related to reduced diuretic use and a prior blood transfusion; she improved with two doses of IV furosemide and resumed her home medications. Diarrhea was evaluated and found not to be due to C. diff, resolving during admission. Her anemia remained stable without transfusion, and she was discharged home with instructions to continue all home medications, complete her antibiotic course, and monitor her weight.
